name: Duplicate QT1.1 — Duplicate of Rejected Claim (Review & Reject) Navigator
description: Resolve the PX_DP1/PX_QT1 hard edits flagging an exact duplicate of a finalized/rejected claim: confirm the LOB via Product, rule out corrected-claim events, compare the duplicate claim, review the history claim, confirm an exact field match and a Resolved-Reject status, review the related claim’s finalization code to confirm it was denied for an authorization that is now available, then reject the current claim with code PX_RDUP00.

steps.name: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT1 hard edits
steps.description: The app will display all edits in the Event Resolution tab, with the PX_DP1 and PX_QT1 hard edits highlighted with an error indication — these are the current events to resolve. The PX_QT1/PX_DP1 events indicate a potential duplicate claim that must be reviewed before processing.
steps.hint: Open the 'Event Resolution' tab. The PX_DP1 and PX_QT1 edits are active and highlighted in red.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT1 hard edits

steps.name: Check the Line of Business via Product field
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS or another Line of Business (LOB) by navigating to the Member Information tab, then the Group Information section, and reviewing the Product field. For ITS claims, the Product field may display values such as Local, National, or ACA. If the Product value is not Local, follow the alternate guidelines. If the Product value is Local, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Product is Local; therefore, the trainee may proceed. Also determine whether the claim was received electronically (alphanumeric) or by paper (numeric) by inspecting the DCN number
steps.hint: Open 'Member Info' and read the Product field under the Group section — it reads 'Local'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Member Info tab to read the Product field.
steps.checklistItem: Check the Line of Business via Product field

steps.name: Check for corrected claim events (PX_PAJ/PX_SCB)
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains corrected claim events by looking for PX_PAJ or PX_SCB events in the Event Resolution tab. If corrected claim events are present, follow the corrected events guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim does not contain corrected claim events, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Return to 'Event Resolution' and scan the All Edits list — there are no PX_PAJ or PX_SCB corrected-claim events.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee revisits the Event Resolution tab to rule out corrected-claim events.

steps.name: Trigger the duplicate-claim comparison
steps.description: Obtain the potential duplicate claim(s) by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab. Review the list of potential duplicate claims displayed in the table. Select the applicable duplicate claim using the radio button in the first column, then click Compare Claim. Once the comparison is initiated, a new section titled Claim Compare Results will appear below the duplicates table. Within this section, review the Show Differences subsection to identify and evaluate any differences between the current claim and the selected potential duplicate claim.
steps.hint: Open Claim Data → Duplicate, select the duplicate line's radio, then click 'Compare Claim'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects the duplicate radio and clicks Compare Claim (dispatches the compare_claim action).

steps.name: Confirm the claim is a duplicate
steps.description: Review the Claim compare results to determine whether the claim is a true duplicate by checking the following fields under the Show differences section: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number under Provider information section, and Attachments under Attachments section. If none of these fields are listed in the Claim compare results, it means the current claim and the history claim are the same — no differences exist, confirming a duplicate. In this scenario, the claim is a duplicate; all accordions (Attachments, Additional claim data, Provider, Claim header, Claim lines) are shown but contain no differing data.
steps.hint: Expand the Claim Compare Results accordions — they show no differing data, confirming a true duplicate.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee reviews the compare-results accordions (dispatches review_duplicate).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the claim is a duplicate

steps.name: Verify the history claim was processed correctly
steps.description: Determine whether the history (duplicate) claim was processed correctly. Click the Open claim detail button to open the history claim. The system displays a message: "In real application, you need to follow guidelines to check if the history claim is processed correctly. In this scenario, consider this history claim is processed correctly." If the history claim was processed incorrectly, it must be adjusted and processed correctly before proceeding; if it was processed correctly, proceed. In this scenario, the history claim is processed correctly, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim and read the advisory message, then proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the history claim detail pop-up (dispatches open_claim_detail).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the history claim was processed correctly

steps.name: Confirm all claim fields match the history claim
steps.description: Compare claim information between the current claim and the history claim to confirm an exact match across all relevant fields: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number, Attachments, Date of service, Place of treatment, Procedure code, Modifiers, Diagnosis codes, National Drug Codes, Billed amount, and Units of occurrence. Note the values of these fields from both claims so you can compare them. To view them side by side, click Confirm match — the values from both the current claim and the history claim will be listed for review. If any field does not match, follow the alternate guidelines; if all fields match, proceed. In this scenario, all information matches, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Open the Matching Duplicate Information panel — every field matches the history claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the matching-field list (dispatches review_matching).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm all claim fields match the history claim

steps.name: Verify history claim is Resolved-Reject
steps.description: Validate whether the history claim is finalized or open by checking the status field on the Summary tab of the history claim (the status is also visible in the rightmost column of the claims listing table). For now, click the Check related status button under duplicate sub-tab of claim data tab — the status of the history claim will be displayed. If the status is Pending-Investigation, the claim is open; if the status is Resolved, the claim is finalized and rejected. In this scenario, the history claim status is Resolved-Reject (already finalized and rejected), so the trainee proceeds to review the denial reason.
steps.hint: Check the related claim status — it reads 'Resolved-Reject', so the history claim is finalized and rejected.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee checks the related claim status (dispatches review_related_status).

steps.name: Verify the denial reason is authorization
steps.description: Validate the reason for the denial of the related claim. In the Search tab → Claims sub-tab, click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim to reopen its detail pop-up, then click the Finalization Code Detail button under the 'Finalization Code — Related Claim Denial Reason' section; read the description that appears to determine the denial reason (for example, code PX_R15270). If the denial reason is authorization-related, check whether the authorization is currently available on the current claim. In this scenario, the related claim was denied for authorization and the authorization is now available on the current claim, so the trainee proceeds to reject the current claim and adjust the original.
steps.hint: Open Search → Claims, click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim, then click 'Finalization Code Detail' — the code reads PX_R15270, an authorization denial.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Finalization Code Detail pop-up inside the history claim detail (dispatches review_finalization_code).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the denial reason is authorization

steps.name: Reject the duplicate claim with code PX_RDUP00
steps.description: Reject the current claim as a duplicate. Navigate to the Action menu and select deny claim. Enter the rejection code "PX_RDUP00" in the rejection code field, then click Submit in the Reject panel.
steps.hint: Action menu → Reject claim. Enter reject code PX_RDUP00 and click Submit in the Reject panel.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Reject (Deny) panel with code PX_RDUP00 (dispatches the deny_claim action).
steps.checklistItem: Reject the duplicate claim with code PX_RDUP00

steps.name: Submit the Reject decision
steps.description: After confirming the Reject panel, click the Submit button to finalize the Reject decision and complete the attempt.
steps.hint: Click the Submit button to finalize the Reject decision.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Reject (Deny) decision with the Submit button.

stepSummaryForResults.name: All fields matched the history claim
